text:
maria: Heads up — spike in pod evicts on eu-west1 GPU pool, ~3% in last 30m. Seeing many preemptions of non-critical jobs. Anyone touching scheduler/taints?

tj: saw alerts. Any correlation with spot reclaim or recent scale-down?

infra-bot: [ALERT] node-pressure: gpu-utilization-surge in eu-west1-gpu (180 pods affected) — 2026-03-18T09:22:10Z

kevin: `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector=status.phase!=Running` output looks grim:
```
NAME                                 READY STATUS   RESTARTS AGE NODE
train-runner-5f9b7d6d9-2zjkl         0/1   Evicted   0      3m  eu-west1-gpu-004
train-runner-5f9b7d6d9-kplmn         0/1   Evicted   0      2m  eu-west1-gpu-004
inference-worker-0                   1/1   Running   0     34m eu-west1-gpu-007
```
kevin: node eu-west1-gpu-004 shows long-lived scratch containers and some daemonsets hogging GPUs; scheduler isn't packing cleanly.

doug: probable fragmentation — lots of small `requests.memory` and whole-GPU device plugin allocation means slack on nodes but unschedulable. Also we rolled out `taint: dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule` on a subset yesterday, could be skewed label/affinity combos.

maria: temporary mitigation idea: run descheduler to evict low-priority noise and consolidate. Alternatively we can relax that taint on a few nodes for non-prod. Thoughts?

tj: quick options: 1) run descheduler `RemovePodsViolatingNodeAffinity` / `RemoveDuplicates` for non-prod, 2) cordon noisy nodes and migrate long-running jobs.

kevin: `kubectl drain` will cause more preemptions if we do it blindly — better to cordon then `kubectl delete pod` for low-priority ones so the scheduler moves them gradually.

ops: FYI we pushed a change to the cluster-autoscaler that prefers tighter binpacking across AZs to save cost; might be causing cross-az skew and making some AZs hot. Rolling that back now.

sre-oncall: opening incident INC-20260318-31. Please post action items and ETA. If this persists we'll escalate to infra pager.

maria: action items: 1) ops revert autoscaler policy (in progress) 2) run descheduler for low-priority pods (doug) 3) cordon eu-west1-gpu-004 and migrate noisy pods (kevin) 4) add GPU free-memory metric alert (tj). I'll update the incident.

tj: ping me when cordoned, I'll run prioritized migrations for critical jobs.

kevin: cordoned eu-west1-gpu-004 (1861234790). Started moving 6 non-prod pods to spill nodes.

maria: thanks — monitoring now. Will watch eviction rate for 15m.

infra-bot: [RESOLVE] node-pressure resolved on eu-west1-gpu at 2026-03-18T09:36:20Z

maria: looks resolved. Follow-up: schedule a deeper grep of scheduler logs and validate GPU device-plugin reports (free memory vs allocatable).

doug: I'll open a short RFC to change request granularity and explore fractional GPU scheduling (or better device plugin reporting).

maria: adding RFC to backlog and tagging for next infra cycle.
